items.title: Broward schools to remain closed Friday; Miami-Dade schools to reopen
items.text: FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla. — Broward County Public Schools will remain closed on Friday as residents continue to deal with flooding. Leer en español Parts of Broward hit particularly hard by torrential rains on Wednesday, prompting the district to cancel classes on Thursday. With Thanksgiving break beginning on Monday, the district said in a social media post that it intends to have schools “safe and ready” by students’ scheduled return date on Nov. 30. “The school calendar will be adjusted for missed instructional time,” the district noted. Meanwhile, Miami-Dade County Public Schools will be back open and business-as-usual on Friday, the district announced.

items.title: Miami-Dade to reopen public schools Friday as torrential rains slow
items.text:
All school activities — including sports — will resume as planned for Friday, the district said in a statement.

Miami-Dade County Public Schools will open its doors Friday after the district gave students and teachers Thursday off due to torrential rains across South Florida.
The school district canceled all school activities Thursday due to the rain, which flooded streets and buildings across Miami-Dade, though the damage was worse to the north in Broward County.
The district, in a statement to social media, announced Thursday afternoon that all activities would resume as usual on Friday. That includes the school day as well as district and regional offices.
The announcement included news on one district event previously slated for Thursday evening. A magnet school information session — “Your Path to Magnet Schools,” hosted at Coral Reef Library — is rescheduled for Dec. 10.
Broward County Public Schools has yet to announce its plans for the school day on Friday. The district closed schools Wednesday and Thursday . Its decision to close schools Wednesday came in the morning when several students were already aboard buses — the timing drew stark criticism from some parents.
Broward County Public Schools wrote on social media Thursday midday that it was “closely monitoring weather conditions.”
“As conditions improve, staff will be assessing the state of our facilities and preparedness to resume operations. The safety of our students and staff remains our highest priority. We continue to work closely with local emergency management officials and will share updates with families and staff as soon as they are available,” the district wrote.
This story was originally published November 19, 2026 at 2:32 PM .
items.desc: All school activities — including sports — will resume as planned for Friday, the district said in a statement.

items.title: Centennial Bank Lends $51M to Expand Miami-Dade Nursing Home
items.text:
The redevelopment will double the number of residential units to 172.

Abraham Shaulson ’s Millennium Management and Manuel Scharf have secured a $51.2 million construction loan to expand a nursing home in Miami-Dade County.
The financing from Centennial Bank covers the Terraces of Hialeah , a 55,518-square-foot facility at 195 West 27th Street , sandwiched between Red Road and the Hialeah Park Casino . The asset was built on a 2.6-acre site between 1950 and 1967.
The redevelopment will increase the property’s footprint to 114,865 square feet and double the number of residential units from 86 to 172, though the number of licensed beds will remain unchanged at 276, according to a representative for the lender.
Portions of the existing structure will be demolished to make space for a surface parking lot and a new three-story facility, while the two-story building facing 28th Street will remain.
Construction, which is expected to take 18 months, will begin after a 60-day notice period for residents, though about 109 beds will remain operational throughout the redevelopment, per Centennial Bank.
Investors are increasingly targeting senior living facilities across South Florida, where the senior population is expected to grow by 2.2 million by 2040, according to state estimates. This month, health care real estate investment trust Welltower has spent over $386 million on nine properties across the region, The Real Deal reported .
Other recent transactions include the Artemis Real Estate Partners ’ $140 million purchase of a 7.2-acre asset and Fortress Investment Group ’s $26 million acquisition of a 118-bed property, both in Delray Beach.
The owners of Terraces of Hialeah could not be reached for comment.
Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com .
items.desc: The redevelopment will double the number of residential units to 172.

items.title: Miami-Dade County celebrates the completion of the South Dade Transit Operations Center
items.text:
Miami-Dade County held a ribbon cutting ceremony for the $250.6 million South Dade Transit Operations Center

Miami-Dade County celebrated the completion of the South Dade Transit Operations Center in Homestead on Wednesday.
The center is designed to accommodate up to 100 articulated battery-electric buses, has dedicated areas for charging, storage, maintenance, dispatch and driver training.
It also includes bus wash stations, parts storage, and also serves as an Emergency Command Center for the Department of Transportation and Public Works to help coordinate the County’s response during major storms and other emergencies.
“This is a proud day for public transportation in Miami-Dade County,” said Mayor Daniella Levine Cava. “This future-ready facility sets a new standard for transit operations not only locally, but nationally. It brings jobs to South Dade and gives us the foundation to deliver cleaner, more reliable transportation for the people who count on it every day.”
The facility itself features solar components, a reclaimed water system and landscaping with more than 45 species of native trees, plants and wildflowers. Miami-Dade County funded the $250.6 million project through the People’s Transportation Plan Bond Program, which is supported by the voter-approved half-cent transportation surtax.
“This state-of-the-art center takes the DTPW into a new era of transit operations,” said DTPW Director and CEO Stacy L. Miller, P.E. “We’ve built a facility that gives our teams the technology to serve riders better today and the room to grow with Miami-Dade. This is how we build a transit system worthy of the trust our riders place in us every day.”
The Homestead center will provide a dedicated home base for Metro Express buses near the South Dade TransitWay. Miami Dade County officials hope that the investment will build a future where cleaner, more dependable transit safely connects more residents to jobs, schools and opportunities.

items.title: 1836: Dade County is created
items.desc: Dade County was created on February 4, 1836, named after Major Francis L. Dade and the Miami River. That same year, Fort Dallas was built and served as a military base during the Second Seminole War.
